title: OmeroExtractor

narrative_arc.enters_knowing: They have OMERO microscopy data and want to understand how to extract it into the pipeline.
narrative_arc.leaves_knowing: What OmeroExtractor does, what its JSON-LD output looks like, the DF-TEM-PAW real-world example, current maturity status.
steps: What OmeroExtractor does — wraps OMERO REST API, produces OME JSON-LD with image metadata and ROIs
Output ontologies: OME, OA, QUDT, PROV-O
Inline: real JSON-LD output snippet for image83 (from test fixtures in local repo)
Real-world example: BAMresearch/DF-TEM-PAW — Hanke et al. 2023
How the output connects to Stage 2 (MapToMethod → RDFConverter)

inline_assets_required.description: First 20 lines of image83.json test fixture — real OMERO image metadata as JSON-LD. Use local fixture at /home/hanke/OmeroExtractor/tests/image83.json.
First 15 lines of image83.ttl test fixture — RDF serialization of OMERO image. Use local fixture.

walkthrough_requirements.step: Note: no public OMERO instance for live testing
walkthrough_requirements.note: Use test fixtures from local repo for inline examples. Label with: # from OmeroExtractor tests/image83.json

primary.name: Data Engineer
knows: Tabular data and data transformation concepts
does_not_know: RDF, triples, or the semantic web stack
YARRRML, RML, or any mapping language
What a named graph or blank node is
primary.goal: Connect data sources, author mappings, and query transformation results.
primary.key_gap: Solid general engineering skills but semantic web is completely foreign. Every RDF/SPARQL/YARRRML concept must be explained from first principles — do not assume any prior semantic knowledge.

secondary.name: Evaluator
secondary.goal: Assess whether DataStack fits their lab or institution — understand outputs and find the right entry point.
